userStories.title: Aura xlsx markitdown plugin — per-row decomposition with YAML frontmatter + plumbing
userStories.description: Today docker/markitdown/Dockerfile sets MARKITDOWN_ENABLE_PLUGINS=False and uses the built-in xlsx converter which emits the workbook as a flat markdown table. The 180-row Italian customer xlsx that broke Aura 2026-05-20 collapses into a single source page with no row-level addressability — Aura search_memory returns the whole source, the LLM must scan 180 rows in context to find one customer, and the heading-subnodes from B04 have nothing to subdivide because there are no `###` headings inside the table. This story ships the plumbing AND the first plugin so subsequent plugins (B08a-d) only add their own converter file. (a) DOCKERFILE: flip MARKITDOWN_ENABLE_PLUGINS=True. Add COPY for a new local Python package directory docker/markitdown/aura-plugins/. RUN pip install --no-deps /tmp/aura-plugins to install it after markitdown[all] so its converters take priority (plugin priority > built-in per markitdown spec). (b) PACKAGE: docker/markitdown/aura-plugins/ with setup.cfg (or pyproject.toml) defining entry_points: `markitdown.plugin = aura:register`. The `aura` package has an __init__.py that imports each per-format converter module and registers it. v0 ships only aura.xlsx_converter. (c) XLSX CONVERTER: aura/xlsx_converter.py implements AuraXlsxConverter(DocumentConverter). accepts xlsx mime + xlsx extension. convert(stream, **kwargs) → DocumentConverterResult with markdown = YAML frontmatter block + one `### Row {N}` heading per non-header data row + bullet list of `- {col_name}: {cell_value}` for each cell. FRONTMATTER fields: workbook_title (filename basename), sheets (list of sheet names), sheet_row_counts (dict sheet→count), author (from xlsx core properties if present, else 'unknown'). HEADER ROW: first row of each sheet is treated as column names, emitted as a `## Sheet: {sheet_name}` H2 heading followed by the column list as a `**Columns**: a, b, c` bold line, NOT as a row entry. DATA ROWS start at row 2. Empty cells render as `- {col_name}: (empty)`. (d) PYTHON DEPS: openpyxl (already a markitdown[all] dep). NO new pip dep. (e) Go SIDE — no change required: the existing client.Convert flow already POSTs bytes to the sidecar and gets back markdown; the new structure is just inside the returned string. Document this explicitly in the commit body. (f) FIXTURE TEST: ship docker/markitdown/aura-plugins/tests/test_xlsx_converter.py — uses an inline xlsx blob (or the existing tika-testEXCEL.xlsx if reachable) and asserts the result has `### Row 1`, `### Row 2`, `**Columns**`, and YAML frontmatter with sheet_row_counts. Pytest runnable as `python -m pytest docker/markitdown/aura-plugins/tests/`. (g) DOCKER BUILD: rebuild the markitdown sidecar after the Dockerfile change; verify the image installs the plugin (RUN python -c 'from markitdown import MarkItDown; m=MarkItDown(enable_plugins=True); print([c.__class__.__name__ for c in m._converters])' shows AuraXlsxConverter in the list).

userStories.title: Aura docx markitdown plugin — per-heading decomposition
userStories.description: Reuses the plugin plumbing shipped in B03. Adds a per-heading converter for docx so each H1/H2/H3 in the Word document becomes a `### {heading_text}` block in the extracted markdown, which the Wave A B04 heading-subnodes parser will then index as separate retrieval nodes. (a) ADD aura/docx_converter.py implementing AuraDocxConverter(DocumentConverter). Accepts docx mime + docx extension. (b) PARSE: use python-docx (already in markitdown[all]). Iterate doc.paragraphs, track current heading_level via paragraph.style.name (`Heading 1` → 1, `Heading 2` → 2, etc.). When entering an H1/H2/H3, start a new `### {heading_text}` block in the output (we always promote H1/H2/H3 from the doc to `###` in markdown so they land in B04's H2/H3 subnode index range; the page itself has a single H1 for the source title). Non-heading paragraphs append to the current heading's body. Tables get rendered as standard markdown tables AFTER the surrounding paragraph. (c) FRONTMATTER: document_title (from doc.core_properties.title or filename basename), author (doc.core_properties.author), created (doc.core_properties.created ISO 8601 or empty), heading_counts (dict {h1:N, h2:N, h3:N}). (d) NO HEADINGS FALLBACK: if the document has zero Heading-styled paragraphs, fall through to the built-in markitdown docx converter (markitdown.converters.DocxConverter) — call it directly so the document is still convertible. Document this with a code comment so future maintainers understand. (e) REGISTER: aura/__init__.py register() adds AuraDocxConverter after AuraXlsxConverter (order doesn't matter for correctness, but keep alphabetical for predictable diff). (f) FIXTURE TEST: docker/markitdown/aura-plugins/tests/test_docx_converter.py with an inline docx blob (use python-docx to generate it in-test, or commit a tiny prebuilt fixture); assert `### Main Heading` appears, frontmatter has heading_counts, non-heading paragraphs are under the right heading.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read the existing aura-plugins package from B03 + B08a. (2) python-pptx: prs = Presentation(stream); prs.slides is a SlideIterator. For each slide, slide.shapes is iterable; shape.has_text_frame + shape.text_frame.text gets body text. (3) Speaker notes: slide.has_notes_slide bool, then slide.notes_slide.notes_text_frame.text. (4) Slide title heuristic: iterate slide.shapes looking for shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE (or fallback to first shape with text). EMPTY SLIDES: a slide with only an image placeholder still gets a heading line but empty body — that's fine, B04 will create a subnode for it (the slide IS the unit). FALLBACK TRIGGER: zero titled AND zero text-bearing shapes across the WHOLE deck → fall through. Single-slide-with-no-content stays in our output (would degenerate to empty body, but the heading marks the slide existed). SCOPE DISCIPLINE: ONLY pptx. No image-extraction (that's not in markitdown[all] anyway). No animation/transition metadata (not useful for retrieval).

userStories.title: Aura html markitdown plugin — per-section decomposition
userStories.description: Reuses the plugin plumbing shipped in B03. Adds a per-section converter for html so each `<section>` / top-level `<article>` / each major `<h1>..<h6>` block becomes a `### {heading_text}` chunk, which the Wave A B04 heading-subnodes parser will then index as separate retrieval nodes. Particularly important for Wikipedia HTML exports which have many `<h2>` section breaks. (a) ADD aura/html_converter.py implementing AuraHtmlConverter(DocumentConverter). Accepts html mime + htm/html extension. (b) PARSE: use BeautifulSoup (already in markitdown[all]). Strategy: walk the DOM in document order. When a heading tag (h1..h6) is encountered, start a new section with `### {heading_text}` (collapse all heading levels to `###` so they fall in B04's H2/H3 subnode range). When a `<section>` or `<article>` element is encountered AND it contains no heading tag of its own, emit `### {section_role_or_aria_label or 'Section N'}`. Non-heading content (p, ul, ol, table, blockquote, pre) renders to markdown via markdownify (if available) OR a tiny inline converter (p→paragraph, ul/ol→bullet list, table→md-table, blockquote→`> `, pre/code→`” code fences```). (c) FRONTMATTER: page_title (from `<title>` tag), description (from `<meta name="description">`), heading_counts (dict h1..h6 → N), section_count (number of `<section>` + `<article>` elements). (d) NO HEADINGS FALLBACK: if the HTML body has ZERO heading tags AND ZERO `<section>`/`<article>` elements, fall through to markitdown.converters.HtmlConverter — single-section blogs / minimal HTML pages still convert. (e) NAV/FOOTER/SCRIPT/STYLE STRIPPING: before any traversal, remove `<script>`, `<style>`, `<nav>`, `<footer>`, `<aside>` (anything that's not content). Document the list of stripped tags. (f) REGISTER: aura/__init__.py adds AuraHtmlConverter (alphabetical: after Epub, before Pptx). (g) FIXTURE TEST: tests/test_html_converter.py with the bench fixture docs/quality-bench/fixtures/wiki-galileo.html — asserts multiple `### ` heading blocks (the Wikipedia article has many sections), page_title in frontmatter = 'Galileo Galilei' (or whatever Wikipedia uses).

(2) BeautifulSoup4: `from bs4 import BeautifulSoup; soup = BeautifulSoup(html_bytes, 'html.parser')`. soup.find_all(['h1','h2','h3','h4','h5','h6']) for headings. TABLE RENDERING: simple HTML tables render to markdown tables; complex tables (rowspan/colspan) collapse to a single-row representation with `|` separators. Document the limitation. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: only html (.html, .htm). No XML, no XHTML if it has a different declaration. No iframe content. PYTHON IMPORT: `from markitdown.converters import HtmlConverter` for fallback. userStories.title: Ingest LLM-prompt v3 — materialize per-section / per-row sub-pages from extracted markdown structure
userStories.description: Today internal/storage/sources/ingest/prompt.go drives a single LLM call that takes the whole extract.md and produces ONE wiki page summarizing the source. After B03 + B08a-d ship, the extract.md for structured formats has `### Row N` / `### Slide N` / `### {heading}` blocks that should each become their OWN wiki sub-page so search_memory + heading subnodes (B04) can return row-level facts. This story updates the ingest prompt + the ingest pipeline to detect the new structure and emit one page per section instead of one page per source. (a) DETECTION: at ingest entry, parse the extract.md for the `### ` heading count. If >= 3 AND the YAML frontmatter present at the top has any of {sheet_row_counts, slide_count, chapter_count, heading_counts, section_count}, treat the source as 'structured' and route to the new sub-page materialization path. Else: existing summary-only path (no change). (b) NEW PIPELINE: for a structured source, emit (i) ONE main wiki page named `source-{source_id}-{normalized_filename}.md` with frontmatter from extract.md + a TOC-like body listing each subsection as a `[[wiki-link]]`; (ii) ONE sub-page per `### ` block named `source-{source_id}-{normalized_filename}-{N}.md` (or `-{anchor}` if the heading has a stable anchor) with frontmatter source_id + parent_slug + heading_text + heading_index + body = the section content.
